subject: EdgeBridge Sprint Zero — K8s Topology, NodePools & Storage charter
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: EdgeBridge Sprint Zero — K8s Topology, NodePools & Storage charter

John —

Thanks for taking time this week. As discussed in the kickoff call, attached is a compact charter for Sprint Zero to align on the on‑prem Kubernetes footprint for your EdgeBridge sites. Goal is to lock the baseline decisions (cluster layout, node pools, storage classes, and networking constraints) so procurement and rack wiring can proceed.

High level asks from CloudBridge we need confirmed before we start provisioning:
- Target cluster size per site (min/max nodes).
- Expected latency-sensitive workloads (inference pods) and their GPU needs.
- Any strict egress IP requirements or BGP peering constraints.

Initial proposals in the attached PDF: a dual‑control-plane HA pair plus 3–6 worker node pools (system/infra/compute/gpu/cache/ephemeral). Storage recommendations use CSI with two SCs: "block‑fast" (Local NVMe with ephemeral eviction policy) and "persistent‑encrypted" (replicated iSCSI/NAS with KMS).

Please review and confirm the bullets below by EOD Wednesday so we can lock the node SKU list with ops: 
1) Minimum 3 worker nodes for HA baseline or 5 if you require even distribution across racks.
2) GPU node pool separate (taints + tolerations) with local NVMe scratch.
3) Persistent volumes via your NAS (NFSv4) with CIFS disabled; if you prefer iSCSI we’ll need blockstore access and multipath config.
4) KMS integration — provide key ARN/service endpoint or confirm Redwood KMS proxy is acceptable.

Attachments: edgebridge-network-map-20261115.pdf (site VLAN and BGP outline), edgebridge-sprint0-checklist-20261115.xlsx (checklist & acceptance gates)

Thanks — I’ll consolidate answers into the intake doc and schedule a short config workshop next week.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@cloudbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-infra@cloudbridge.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EdgeBridge Sprint Zero — K8s Topology, NodePools & Storage charter

Vivek —

Thanks, got it. Quick answers to your bullets (ops team copied):
- Cluster size: prefer baseline 5 worker nodes per site; we have two racks so that maps to 2/3 split for anti‑affinity.
- Workloads: two classes — latency critical (inference) and batch (analytics). Latency critical needs 4 x A10‑class GPUs per site.
- Egress / Networking: we need static egress IPs per site for downstream licenses (can provide list during procurement). BGP peering planned with our core; we will share ASN and VLAN IDs by Tuesday.
- Storage: primary backing will be an on‑site NAS exported over NFSv4 (auth via client IPs). We can pilot iSCSI on one site if Redwood recommends for PV performance.
- KMS: We can expose a customer KMS endpoint (internal) but would like Redwood to support a proxy mode for credential exchange.

We reviewed the PDF and checklist — one note on monitoring: Ops will need a central Logstash/Elasticsearch collector; will Redwood ship a fluentd/collector DaemonSet, or do you expect us to forward?

I’ll gather the ASN/VLAN/egress IP list and send by Tuesday EOD.

— John
John Sullivan
Director, Infrastructure
CloudBridge Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, John Sullivan <john.sullivan@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EdgeBridge Sprint Zero — K8s Topology, NodePools & Storage charter

John / Vivek —

Nice to see the clarifications. A few operational details from our side to make the acceptance gates unambiguous:
- NodePool definitions: we will create YAML templates for the following pools: control-plane (managed as static VMs), system (small CPU, taint), infra (monitoring, logging, ingress), compute (general), gpu (A10 class), and ephemeral-cache (local NVMe journal). Each template will include resource requests/limits + evictionPriority.
- StorageClasses: we recommend two SCs out of the box: fast-block (CSI using local multipath to NVMe) and standard-persistent (NFSv4 w/ root squash off only if necessary). PV reclaim policy: Retain for persistent, Delete for ephemeral.
- Network: we'll expect L2 VLANs and an IP pool for kube‑service/external IP allocation; please provide ranges and whether HAProxy/MetalLB will need specific BGP communities.
- Backups: snapshot plan — daily snapshots for DB pods, weekly full replication for important PVs (retention 30 days). We'll include a CRD to mark critical PVs.
- Monitoring: Redwood will deliver a tenant Fluent Bit DaemonSet and a small ES index template. Ops team can elect to accept forwarded logs to their central collector; we’ll provide TLS + CA bundle.

Requesting two quick confirmations from CloudBridge:
1) Will you allow privileged CSI node-plugin (we sign an SLA for secure mode) or do we move to an agent-less backup path?
2) Provide the NTP servers and whether we should expect network time restrictions inside your firewall.

If we get both confirmations, I’ll publish the Sprint Zero inventory and open a rubric for the preflight acceptance (rack wiring, KMS tests, CSI attach/detach validation, NFS mount scalability).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: edgebridge-sprint0-checklist-20261115.xlsx]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EdgeBridge Sprint Zero — K8s Topology, NodePools & Storage charter

John —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Good to see alignment. Quick answers to your monitoring question: Redwood will include the Fluent Bit DaemonSet + Elasticsearch index mapping as Marissa noted. We can either ship logs to your cluster‑local ELK or forward to your central instance; Marissa will add forwarding instructions to the checklist.

Confirmations we have from Redwood now:
- CSI driver requires privileged node plugin for multipath/local NVMe. We will document the minimal RBAC and seccomp profile and run it in a hardened mode.
- KMS proxy: yes, we support a short‑lived token proxy to your KMS endpoint; security will do a one‑time key exchange during preflight.

Next steps:
1) John — please send ASN/VLAN/egress IP list + NTP hosts by EOD Tuesday.
2) Marissa — publish the inventory + preflight rubric once the NTP/KMS bits are added.
3) I’ll schedule the config workshop for Thursday (30 minutes) to approve node SKUs and acceptance tests.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting the first site into provisioning next month.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

[Attachments sent: edgebridge-network-map-20261115.pdf, edgebridge-sprint0-checklist-20261115.xlsx]
